L0: # Rapid agent swarms. Make any agentic workflow exponentially faster.
L1: 
L2: Funded by Y Combinator
L3: 
L4: 【0†Sign in】 【1†Install the CLI】
L5: 
L6: Get started
L7: ## Run your first agent swarm.
L8: 
L9: A swarm splits your task across coding agents, each in its own sandbox. They work in parallel, then merge into one patch or pull request.
L10: 
L11: Play · 0:37
L12: 
L13: 37 seconds, with sound and captions: from install to an applied patch. 【2†Step-by-step guide →】
L14: 
L15: `npm install -g @acyclic-labs/cli` [Button: Copy]
L16: 
L17: macOS and Linux. Installs the `acyclic` command. No Node? `curl -fsSL https://acyclic.dev/install.sh | sh` fetches the binary with a verified checksum (【3†read it first】).
L18:   1. ### 1. Sign in
L19: 
L20: Opens your browser to approve this device. One login lasts 90 days.
L21: 
L22:     acyclic swarm login --site https://acyclic.dev
L23: 
L24:   2. ### 2. Describe the task
L25: 
L26: Run it inside your project: `--dir .` uploads your working files (no history, no secrets). `--watch` follows the agents live.
L27: 
L28:     acyclic swarm run --task "fix the flaky test in tests/api" --dir . --watch
L29: 
L30:   3. ### 3. Take the result
L31: Apply the merged patch to your checkout, or open a pull request from the dashboard.
L32: 
L33:     acyclic swarm pull <swarm-id> --apply
L34: 
L35: Prefer not to install anything? Start a swarm from the 【4†dashboard】 or connect a coding agent over 【5†MCP】. Full reference: 【6†CLI guide】.
L36: 
L37: Talk to us
L38: ## Scale agent swarms to tasks that are too big for one agent.
L39: 
L40: Acyclic runs large tasks as a swarm: fan work out across many agents, fork the ones worth exploring, watch every branch as it runs, and keep only the results you verified.
L41: 
L42: We're onboarding teams gradually, starting with those that already run agents in volume. Tell us what you're running and one of the founders will set up a short conversation about scaling it.
L43:   * →Startups building domain-specific agents that need to run at scale
L44:   * →Companies already operating swarms of agents in production
L45:   * →Teams running many Claude Code or Codex sessions on large codebases
